findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (with a proving test) that exercises the assembled outbound path (outbound_differ -> outbound_mutation_builders -> _diff_comments) and asserts the breadcrumb mutation is produced when local_parents/local_ticket_types are wired, so the threading itself is covered.
evidence: Scope: 'outbound_mutation_builders.py — thread local_parents/local_ticket_types into the _diff_comments call' and 'outbound_differ.py — build local_parents {ticket_id -> parent_id} ... and thread it down'
Testing: 'In-process unit tests over _build_parent_breadcrumb/_breadcrumb_target (stub binding store, synthetic snapshots; pure logic).'
All ACs cite test_parent_breadcrumb.py; none exercise the differ-assembled call chain.
findings.finding: The Scope lists production wiring deliverables (thread local_parents/local_ticket_types through outbound_mutation_builders._diff_comments call and build local_parents in outbound_differ), but all five acceptance criteria are verified only by unit tests over the pure cluster (_build_parent_breadcrumb/_breadcrumb_target) with stub binding store and synthetic snapshots. No criterion exercises the assembled path outbound_differ -> outbound_mutation_builders -> _diff_comments to prove the breadcrumb is actually emitted when the real differ runs.
findings.location: Scope (outbound_mutation_builders.py / outbound_differ.py bullets) vs Acceptance Criteria + Testing
scenarios: The pure cluster works but a threading bug in outbound_mutation_builders passes None (or the wrong map) so the breadcrumb never emits in production, and every unit test still passes green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that constructs the differ inputs (a type-collapsed bound parent + bound ancestor) and asserts _diff_comments returns exactly one breadcrumb add mutation carrying the tag and RECONCILER_MARKER, covering the map-building/threading in outbound_differ and outbound_mutation_builders.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency assumption for append-once: confirm reconciler passes are serialized per-child (or describe how a racing pass reading a stale comment list is prevented from a duplicate breadcrumb add).
evidence: "scan the resolved comments for the tag; if present, emit nothing (first-writer-wins, stable across passes"
The resolved list is '(snapshot, or one bounded client.get_comments live fetch)' — a stale snapshot would not reflect a breadcrumb added by an in-flight concurrent pass.
findings.finding: The append-once dedup is a check-then-act (scan resolved comments for the tag, then emit if absent) over a comment list resolved from a snapshot or a single live fetch; if two reconciler passes run against the same child before the first breadcrumb is visible in the resolved list, both could pass the tag check and post duplicate breadcrumbs. The plan asserts append-once 'stable across passes' but does not state whether passes are serialized per-child or how a concurrent/racing pass is prevented from a double-add.
scenarios: Two overlapping reconciler passes on the same child each read a pre-breadcrumb comment list and each post a breadcrumb — the 'no conflicting duplicate' guarantee is violated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a negative test pinning the parity branches: a present 'epic' parent and a parent-absent child each yield zero breadcrumb mutations.
evidence: Parity prose enumerates three outcome classes but ACs only pin the type-collapsed-bound and no-bound-ancestor cases.
"a present \"epic\" parent triggers neither; a parent absent from the map triggers neither" — asserted, no cited test.
findings.finding: The drift-condition parity section describes distinct gate branches (present non-epic incl. blank '' ⇒ breadcrumbed; present 'epic' ⇒ neither; parent absent ⇒ neither), but the enumerated acceptance-criteria tests cover only the bound-type-collapsed-emitted case, the intervening-unbound case, and the no-bound-ancestor omitted case. There is no named test asserting the negative branches (a present 'epic' parent produces no breadcrumb; a parent absent from local_ticket_types produces no breadcrumb), so the parity claim is stated but not test-pinned.
scenarios: A future change to the gate that accidentally breadcrumbs epic-parented children (or parent-absent children) would pass the current test list undetected.
